title: Term 1 and 2 Examination
instructions: This paper covers the work of Terms 1 and 2.
This question paper consists of 4 questions. Answer ALL the questions.
Read each question carefully before you answer it.
Show your working, and round your answers as each question asks.

sections.title: QUESTION 1: Numbers and Calculations in Context

questions.prompt: A school must transport 230 learners. Each bus holds 65 learners. How many buses are needed?
Calculate 12% of R850.
The price of bread rose from R16 to R18. Calculate the percentage increase.
A car travels 270 km in 3 hours. What is its average speed?
Which is better value: 750 ml of juice for R18,99 or 2 ℓ for R45,99? Show your working.
questions.memo:
✓ 750 ml: R18,99 ÷ 0,75 = R25,32 per litre (1)
✓ 2 ℓ: R45,99 ÷ 2 = R23,00 per litre (1)
✓ 2 ℓ is better value (1)

questions.prompt: Three friends invest R2 000, R3 000 and R5 000 in a business and share a profit of R4 500 in the ratio of their investments. How much does each receive?
A bakkie uses 9 ℓ per 100 km. Diesel costs R22,80 per litre. Calculate the fuel cost of a 250 km journey.
A plumber charges $C = 350 + 200h$ (rand), where $h$ is hours worked. What is the cost of a 3-hour job?
Using $C = 350 + 200h$, how many hours were worked if the bill was R1 550?
Which is an example of direct proportion?
options: Speed and travel time for a fixed distance
Number of tickets bought and total cost
Number of people sharing a pizza and slices each
Workers and days to finish a job

questions.prompt: The graph of a direct proportion always passes through the origin.

Option A: R100 per month plus R1,50 per minute. Option B: R2,50 per minute with no monthly fee. Find the number of minutes for which both cost the same, and say which option is cheaper for 150 minutes.
questions.memo:
✓ $100 + 1{,}5m = 2{,}5m$ (1)
✓ $m = 100$ minutes (1)
✓ At 150 min: A = R325, B = R375 (1)
✓ Option A is cheaper (1)

questions.prompt: Describe the shape of the graph of an inverse proportion.
questions.memo:
✓ A curve, not a straight line (1)
✓ that gets closer to the axes but never touches them (1)

sections.title: QUESTION 3: Finance: Income, Expenditure and Budgets

questions.prompt: Take-home pay after deductions is called…
Calculate the employee's UIF contribution on a gross salary of R12 400.
Which is a fixed expense?
Gross pay is R8 600 and total deductions are R1 340. Calculate net pay.
If expenditure is greater than income, the budget has a deficit.
Classify each item.
A security guard earns R65 per hour for 40 hours a week, and overtime at 1,5 times the normal rate. Calculate his gross pay for a week in which he works 46 hours.
A learner makes 40 cupcakes at a total cost of R180 and sells them at R8 each. Calculate the profit if all are sold, and the minimum number she must sell to break even.
questions.memo:
✓ Income 40 × R8 = R320, profit R140 (1)
✓ Break even: R180 ÷ R8 = 22,5 (1)
✓ She must sell 23 cupcakes (1)

questions.prompt: A family spends R3 150 on groceries out of a net income of R18 000. What percentage of income is this?
